annotations.text:
1–2 · SIGNING IN
Every login state the server can actually produce: empty, client-side field validation, rejected credentials, in flight, and authenticated-but-not-linked-to-a-store.

App name is a placeholder

"MyShop" appears only on the splash and login. The customer invoice carries the SHOP's name and address, never the app's — so renaming the product later touches two screens and no customer-facing output.

3–4 · FIRST RUN AND BLOCKED
After the owner resets a password, the temporary one gets the employee in once and the app forces a new one. 4a is the reference sheet for all four block reasons and what each role is told.

⚠ STATUS VOCABULARY — needs a decision

These screens use four statuses: Pending → In progress → Ready → Delivered.

The backend has THREE (prisma/schema.prisma:29): PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED. There is no Ready and no Delivered.

The designs keep your four because you specified them twice. Shipping them needs the enum extended and a migration; otherwise Ready and Delivered both collapse onto COMPLETED and the 9-series loses a step.

5–8 · TAKING A SALE
Tap Add: a kg field for weighed services, a − / + stepper for per-piece. Cards now show real slab pricing.

5c is how a mis-added service or mistyped weight gets fixed — without it there was no way back. 5d clears the whole sale.

Checkout takes the FULL amount or nothing: Cash, UPI, or Pay on delivery.

9 · ORDERS — THE COLLECT-AND-DELIVER LOOP
Opening an order always pushes a full independent screen. Both actions on it are dialogs:

9d Update status offers Pending / In progress / Ready. Delivered is never set by hand.
9e Collect payment takes Cash or UPI for the whole amount — that one action marks the order delivered and creates the invoice.
9g carries care instructions, the delivery commitment (overdue / due today / upcoming) and the full status history with who did what.

Invoice rule

Created only when the order is collected in full — the same moment it becomes delivered (9e). Never earlier.

Backend changes: getOrCreateOrderInvoice() creates on any view request today; it must refuse until the order is settled. And recordPaymentAction is owner-only — that guard must be relaxed for 9e.

═══ SHOP OWNER ═══
Same system as the employee app — white surfaces, 56px app bars, centred dialogs, full-screen detail. Four tabs instead of two. New Sale is identical to the employee's (5a–8) and is not redrawn.

A1–A6 daily: dashboard, its reports half, the reporting-period picker, store switcher, and the two subscription states.
A7–A8 orders: same screens as staff, plus who took the order.
A9–A20 everything an employee never sees.

The owner's order screens are deliberately the SAME as the employee's, plus staff attribution — one order detail, one collect dialog, one status dialog to build. The role changes what is reachable, not how an order behaves.

Two different profiles

A18 Store profile — name, address, phone — is the invoice header, the only business identity a customer sees.

A19 Your details — name, username, email, phone — is the person. Customers never see it. The web app puts both on one Profile page; on mobile they are separate because only one of them is customer-facing.

Checked against the running web app

Everything the web workspace does at mobile width is now covered, except two deliberate restrictions you set: no partial payments (the web has a free "Received now" amount and a separate Record-a-payment amount), and no per-order notes field at the customer step — though notes still DISPLAY on 9g as Care instructions.

Still web-only by design: the platform-admin sign-in link on login, which belongs to Super Admin, not this app.

═══ V2 — PROPOSED REDESIGN ═══
A separate exploration. Nothing on the left has been touched; v1 remains the approved set.

What changed, and why:
• Page ground is a faint cool tint (#f7f9fc) so white cards read as objects rather than outlined regions. This reverses the "pure white" instruction — deliberately, to be judged side by side.
• Every row leads with a tinted TYPE tile instead of an order code. Laundry has no product photos, so service type carries the colour: wash = blue, dry clean = violet, iron = amber.
• Lists group themselves by urgency (Overdue / Due today / Upcoming) instead of relying on the user to pick a filter.
• Four dashboard figures collapse into ONE card, freeing ~100px — which is what makes room for the status strip and To-collect card above the fold.
• V1 Today is new: the screen that answers "what do I need to finish right now?". Nothing in v1 answers that.

Adapted from the StayFlow operations app's widget vocabulary, not copied from it. The three consumer laundry references were deliberately NOT followed — photography, greetings and promo cards cost space a counter tool cannot spare.
